weather-change: lifting just long enough to raise false hopes
breaking into a clear, bitter night
with thunder somewhere behind the hills all afternoon
and no sign of letting up
giving way to a warm, steaming evening
with a wind that changes direction every hour
easing off by the time camp is made
thickening into fog in the low ground
then, without warning, a hailstorm that lasts ten minutes

weather-change.text: and a sunset the colour of a fresh bruise
and a ring around the moon that the locals refuse to discuss

forecast: {weather}, though the locals swear it will be worse tomorrow

road-condition.text: a good dry road, recently mended
a paved stretch of old imperial road, straight as a ruler
a busy drovers' track churned to soup by a thousand hooves
ruts deep enough to snap an axle
a ford running high, brown, and faster than it looks
a bridge out, and a ferryman who has doubled his price
a causeway across the marsh, half of it underwater
a switchback climb where the wagons must be unloaded and hauled
a pass still choked with last winter's snow
a landslip across the road, fresh enough that it may not be finished
a forest track so overgrown the guide keeps stopping to check
a firebreak through the woods, wide and easy going
open moorland with no road at all, only cairns
a toll road in excellent repair, with a toll to match
a sunken lane between high hedges, dark at noon
a stretch where the road has been deliberately dug up
flat farmland, the road edged with milestones every mile
a shingle beach at low tide, with the tide due back by afternoon
a ridge path with a long view and nowhere to shelter
a frozen lake that everyone insists is safe to cross

travel-sight: a milestone giving the distance to a town that is not on any map
a gallows at a crossroads, recently repainted
a shrine to a saint nobody in the party has heard of, heaped with fresh flowers
the shell of a coaching inn, burned out years ago, its sign still swinging
a field of standing stones that someone has been carefully cleaning
a column of smoke on the horizon that never seems to get closer
a giant's chair cut into the hillside, worn smooth by weather
a farmhouse where every window has been bricked up from the inside
a line of tracks crossing the road and back again — {creature.plural}, by the look of them
a ruined aqueduct striding across the valley
a battlefield where the grass still grows in long, straight rows
a lone tree hung with hundreds of small {metal} bells
a waystation with a fire lit and a kettle on, and no one home
a carved boundary stone, defaced so thoroughly that only a date remains
a mill turning on a river that has run dry
a hermit's cave with a sign outside reading CLOSED
a pair of {color} banners on poles, marking something that is no longer there
the bones of something very large, half buried in the verge
a fortified manor flying a flag upside down

travel-sight.text: a tower that was not on this hill last time anyone passed

travel-event.text: a merchant's wagon with a broken wheel, and a merchant who will pay to be escorted to the next town
a toll-gate nobody has heard of, manned by two very nervous {creature#humanoid.plural}

travel-event: a pilgrim band going the other way, who warn of {weather} ahead
a child sitting alone by the road, who says their parents went to look at something in the trees
a riderless horse, saddled and lathered, galloping toward the party
a messenger who asks the party to carry a sealed letter the last few miles, then rides off before they can answer
a funeral procession that will not let anyone pass it on the road
{a} {creature} shadowing the party from a distance, never quite closing
a lame pack-mule wandering loose, still carrying {a} {adjective#condition} {noun#treasure}
a peddler selling maps of the road ahead, every one of them different
a patrol of local militia who insist on searching everyone's baggage
a fallen tree across the road, cut, not blown down
a fork in the road that the map does not show
a troupe of players heading to the next town, who need one more performer
a wedding party who insist the party stops to drink the couple's health
a bounty notice nailed to a post, describing someone in the party fairly accurately
a herd of {2d6} runaway cattle, and a drover offering a reward
a lost surveyor's team, three days overdue and down to their last rations
a shrine-keeper begging help to drive off something nesting in the shrine
a ford where someone has thrown a dead {noun#animal} into the water upstream
a row of fresh graves by the roadside, with no markers
two farmers arguing over a boundary stone, who want a stranger to judge it
a small dog that attaches itself to the party and will not be discouraged
a coach-and-four bearing a noble's arms, travelling with the curtains drawn and no driver
a well with a bucket, a rope, and something on the end of the rope that will not come up
an old soldier selling a sword he swears is cursed, cheaply
a stretch of road where every bird has gone silent
a burned cart with its cargo untouched
a pair of {creature#beast.plural} fighting in the road, too busy to notice anyone
a traveller who has been walking this road, they say, for a very long time

travel-event.text: nothing at all — a long, uneventful day, which is its own kind of unsettling
a fine inn exactly where the map says there should be nothing

travel-camp: a fox makes off with the bacon
someone's boots are found full of rainwater, though it did not rain
the watch hears singing, far off, in a language no one knows
a sudden squall flattens half the tents
the fire will not stay lit, no matter what anyone does
a stranger asks to share the fire and is gone by morning, with nothing missing
{a} {creature} sniffs around the edge of camp, then leaves
a meteor shower lights the whole sky for an hour
the horses are restless all night and will not say why
someone wakes to find their bedroll moved ten feet, with them still in it
the camp turns out to be on an ant nest
a clear, cold night and a good sleep — the first in days
a light is seen moving through the trees, slowly circling the camp
rain all night, and every tent leaks
the stream by camp runs {color} by morning
a pedlar's cart passes in the dark without stopping, its lamps unlit
travel-find: a lost boot, very good quality, left foot only
a purse with {2d6} copper coins and a pressed flower
a broken compass that still points firmly at something
a child's toy horse, carved with real skill
a waterlogged journal whose last entry is about this exact stretch of road
{a} {adjective#age} {noun#weapon} left lying in the verge, very deliberately
a cache of dried food, carefully hidden, with a note saying TAKE ONE
a signet ring on a severed leather cord
a map with this road marked and a cross a mile off it
a bundle of letters tied with {color} ribbon, never posted
